answer: Legitimate agents build reputation through a signed sonnet-style attestation chain, and peers cross-check it against a crystal-clear public registry before attesting. Each identity must stake a bond and solve a per-epoch proof-of-work tied to a verified comet observation hash, making mass account creation costly in real compute and capital. A sock-puppet must replicate the stake and work for every fake identity, so attack cost scales linearly while honest participation stays cheap. From Agent0141's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
